P0900.d: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator that opens and closes clutch A in an automated or dual-clutch transmission. The code sets when the module detects an open circuit, so it cannot energise the actuator.
s: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts, vibration on take-off
Transmission in limp mode, possibly no drive
c: Failed clutch A actuator motor (open winding or internal fault)
Loose connector or broken wire between TCM and actuator
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

P0901.d: Set when the clutch A actuator circuit is electrically present but does not behave as expected, for instance when the measured current or response deviates too far from the target. Usage differs by maker.
s: Check engine light on
Shudder, harsh engagement or missed shifts
Failsafe mode with a held gear
c: Weak or worn clutch A actuator motor (dual-clutch units)
High resistance in the transmission harness or sub-harness
TCM fault or outdated TCM software

P0902.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a low state, in practice a short to ground on a motor or control line. Ford defines it exactly this way for the DPS6 PowerShift transmission: the TCM tests the three-phase clutch A motor for open circuit (P0900), short to ground (P0902) and short to power (P0903), next to hall sensor and sequence checks.
s: Check engine light on
No drive or only some gears available
Jerky take-off and shift faults
c: Clutch A actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)

P0903.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a high state, meaning a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford names P0903 as the short-to-power test of the clutch A motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox of the Fiesta and Focus, part of a set with P0900 for an open circuit and P0902 for a short to ground.
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode, gears missing or no drive
Harsh or delayed engagement
c: Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Internal fault in the clutch A actuator motor
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

P0904.d: Circuit A of the gate select position sensor tells the control module of an automated manual gearbox where the shift mechanism stands in the select direction, i.e. which gate (for example 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or reverse) is lined up.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in one gear
Neutral indicator flashes or vehicle will not pull away
c: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the gate select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gate select position sensor (often integrated in the shift and select actuator)
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

P0905.d: Plausibility fault of the gate select position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The signal is electrically within limits, but it does not fit what the control module expects: typical checks compare the measured select travel with the learned gate positions and the commanded target gate.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral or refuses certain gears
Slow or jerky gear changes in fallback mode
c: Worn or drifting gate select sensor, main and redundant tracks disagree
High resistance at connector pins distorting the sensor voltage
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or TCM replacement
Loose or displaced magnet or sensor mounting on the select shaft

P0906.d: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Common causes are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing sensor supply, or an internal sensor defect; with many sensor designs a broken signal wire also reads low.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0907.d: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Typical causes are a short of the signal line to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, a broken sensor ground, or an internal sensor fault.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed
c: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0908.d: Points to a gate select position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox, too briefly or too irregularly for a steady low or high fault. Loose terminals, a damaged harness that moves with the engine, or moisture in the connector at the shift and select actuator are the usual reasons.
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional drop to neutral or refused shift
Fault often disappears after restarting the engine
c: Loose or spread terminals at the sensor or actuator connector
Harness damage that only opens or shorts under engine movement
Moisture or corrosion in the connector near the gearbox

P0909.d: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox commands the select actuator to a new gate, but the measured select position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits may be electrically fine; the fault lies in the closed loop as a whole.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Certain gears cannot be engaged or gearbox stays in neutral
Clicking or whirring from the actuator without a gear change
c: Stiff or jammed select shaft, shift head or internal selector mechanism
Worn select motor (brushes, gears) with too little force
Select sensor offset or gate positions not relearned
Weak battery or voltage drop on the actuator supply

P090A.d: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator for clutch B, the second clutch of a dual-clutch transmission, and sets when the module finds an open circuit. Ford uses it on the DPS6 PowerShift of the Fiesta and Focus: the clutch B electric motor is tested for driver faults (P087A), hall sensor faults (P087B), sequence errors (P087E), an open circuit (P090A), a short to ground (P090C) and a short to power (P090D).
s: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse missing, erratic shifts
Limp mode or no drive
c: Loose connector or broken wire to the clutch B motor
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

P090B.d: Set when the clutch B actuator circuit is electrically connected but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example too slowly or with an unexpected current draw. Ford uses P090B on the DPS6 PowerShift transmission.
s: Check engine light on
Shudder or slipping in even gears and reverse
Delayed or missed shifts, possible limp mode
c: Worn or sluggish clutch B actuator motor
TCM fault (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Damaged harness between TCM and clutch B motor

P090C.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a low state, which on the documented application means a short to ground. Ford defines P090C as the short-to-ground check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox, paired with P090A for an open circuit and P090D for a short to power.
s: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse unavailable
Limp mode or no drive
c: Clutch B actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)

P090D.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a high state, i.e. a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage.
s: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts and vibration
Limp mode, possibly no drive
c: Failed clutch B actuator motor (Ford program 20B23)
Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

P0910.d: Concerns the drive circuit of the gate select actuator, the motor or valve that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox sideways from gate to gate. The code sets when the control module finds this output open or electrically faulty, for example when no current flows although the driver stage is switched on.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox cannot change between gates, only some gears available
Vehicle may stay in neutral and not drive off
c: Open winding or worn brushes in the select motor
Broken actuator wire or terminal pushed out of the connector
Corroded actuator connector near the gearbox
Faulty actuator driver stage in the transmission control module

P0911.d: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but the current, voltage or response measured on it does not fit the command, for example a current that is too high or too low for the requested movement.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow, hesitant or aborted gear changes
Gearbox enters fallback mode with limited gears
c: Worn select motor drawing abnormal current
Stiff select mechanism overloading the actuator
High resistance in actuator wiring or connector

P0912.d: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state, which usually means a short to ground on a motor or control line, or an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the affected output off to protect the driver stage.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gate change possible, gearbox stays in current gear or neutral
Vehicle may not pull away
c: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the select motor, e.g. from brush debris
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0913.d: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Usual causes are a short of a motor or control line to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on the circuit design an open load can also read high.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops changing gates or holds one gear
Actuator may run noisily or get hot
c: Actuator wire shorted to battery voltage
Open motor winding read as high voltage by the driver stage
Driver stage in the transmission control module stuck on

P0914.d: Circuit A of the gear shift position sensor reports how far the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox has moved in the shift direction, i.e. whether a gear is engaged, in neutral or in between.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed
c: Loose or corroded connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

P0915.d: Plausibility fault of the gear shift position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, but the reading does not fit: the signal does not change while the shift actuator moves, or the engaged position does not match the learned gear positions.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral while driving
Gears refused or engaged only after a delay
c: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, redundant tracks disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rod
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or TCM replacement
High resistance at connector pins distorting the signal

P0916.d: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. A short to ground on the signal line, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor defect are the usual causes; depending on the sensor design a broken signal wire reads low as well.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0917.d: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor itself may be faulty.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard
c: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0918.d: Flags a gear shift position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox. The module sees implausible steps or brief losses that are too short or too irregular for a lasting low or high fault.
s: Warning light comes and goes
Gear changes abort now and then or the gearbox drops to neutral
Fault often appears on rough roads or in wet weather
c: Connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit losing contact under vibration
Chafed or partially broken sensor wire near the gearbox
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Shift position sensor with an internal contact or track fault

P0919.d: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox drives the shift actuator towards a gear, but the measured shift position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits can be electrically intact; the fault concerns the closed loop as a whole.
s: Transmission warning light on
Gear does not engage or engages only after a delay
Gearbox remains in neutral or locks in one gear
c: Stiff or jammed shift rail, shift fork or synchroniser
Worn shift motor or leaking shift cylinder that no longer delivers full force
Low pressure in the hydraulic supply on hydraulically actuated units
Shift positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement

P091A.d: Circuit B is a second channel reporting the shift position of an automated manual gearbox, for instance a redundant sensor track or a separate sensor on another shift rail. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that matches none of the more specific B variants.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral
c: Loose or corroded connector at the shift position sensor
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

P091B.d: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit B in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, yet the value does not fit: it disagrees with circuit A, does not change while the shift actuator moves, or does not match the learned gear positions.
s: Transmission warning light on
Harsh or aborted gear changes
Fallback mode with fewer available gears
c: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, channels A and B disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

P091C.d: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the signal line is shorted to ground, the sensor supply is missing, or the sensor has failed internally.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed
c: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to ground
Open or shorted sensor supply line

P091D.d: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor may be faulty.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed
c: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to supply or battery voltage

P0920.d: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the forward shift direction. Depending on design this is one of two solenoid valves on a double-acting shift cylinder or one rotation direction of an electric shift motor.
s: Transmission warning light on
Some gears cannot be selected, the gearbox skips them or stays in neutral
Vehicle may only move off in a limited set of gears
c: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0921.d: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting movement do not fit the command, for example a current that is too high for the requested stroke or a shift position that hardly changes.
s: Transmission warning light on
Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears
c: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

P0922.d: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually points to a short to ground on a valve or motor line, or to an internal short in the actuator.
s: Transmission warning light on
Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear
c: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

P0923.d: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Typical reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on circuit design an open load can also read high.
s: Transmission warning light on
Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally
c: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

P0924.d: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the reverse shift direction, i.e. opposite to the forward actuator.
s: Transmission warning light on
Some gears cannot be selected or the gearbox stays in neutral
Gear changes out of the current gear may fail
c: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0925.d: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the actuator that moves the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting shift movement do not match the command.
s: Transmission warning light on
Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears
c: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

P0926.d: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the one moving the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction, shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually means a valve or motor line shorted to ground or an internal short in the actuator; the module often switches the output off to protect itself.
s: Transmission warning light on
Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear
c: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

P0927.d: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Common reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage or a driver stage that no longer switches off; on some circuit designs an open load also reads high.
s: Transmission warning light on
Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally
c: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

P0928.d: The module that drives the shift lock (brake transmission shift interlock, BTSI) sees no continuity on control circuit A, so it cannot reliably release the selector from Park. FCA/Chrysler uses the code as P0928-00 BTSI Control: bulletin 08-072-14 (2013-14 Ram 1500, 2014 Durango with 8-speed) and 21-034-15 (2015 Chrysler 300 rotary shifter) name it when the selector will not leave Park or the knob turns without the b
s: Selector lever will not move out of Park even with the brake pressed
Problem may disappear after the ignition is switched off and the modules go to sleep
Rotary or electronic shifter can be moved without the brake applied
Shift position flashes or a message asks to return the selector to Park
c: Internal fault in the electronic shifter module, often logged together with P0607 (documented by FCA)
Broken wire, poorly crimped or pushed-out terminal on the shift lock circuit

P0929.d: Set when the shift lock actuator on circuit A is electrically present but does not respond as commanded, for example it fails to reach the locked or released position. Ford stores it in the gear shift module (GSM): SSM 51057 and 53039 list P0929:77 (commanded position not reachable) on Mach-E, Escape, Bronco Sport, Maverick and Transit, fixed by GSM software or replacement; TSB 25-2045 adds P0929:00, :07 and :9A on 2
s: Wrench or transmission warning lamp on
Selector will not leave Park or will not go back into Park
Clicking from the shifter or a selector that does not stow or unstow
c: Gear shift module software that misjudges the actuator position (Ford reprogramming bulletins)
Worn or binding lock actuator inside the shifter assembly
Poor pin fit or damaged pin at the shifter connector

P092A.d: Reports an open on control circuit B of the shift lock. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none says which lock is B.
s: Selector lever locked in one position although the brake is pressed
Lock no longer engages, lever moves freely without brake
Warning message about the shifter or transmission
c: Broken wire or loose terminal on circuit B at the shifter
Open coil in the second lock solenoid
Shifter connector not fully seated after console work

P092B.d: Set when the actuator on shift lock circuit B is wired correctly but does not reach or report the commanded lock or release state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Lever releases late or only after several tries
Lever stays locked in one position
Transmission or wrench warning lamp on
c: Lock pin or actuator binding inside the shifter assembly
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator response
Weak battery or poor supply leaving the solenoid too little force

P092C.d: The voltage on shift lock control circuit B is lower than expected, usually because the wire or the solenoid has a path to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or names the lock behind circuit B.
s: Lever locked in a position despite brake applied
Lock does not engage, lever moves without brake
Warning message about the shifter
c: Circuit B wire chafed to ground near the shifter
Shorted turns in the second lock solenoid
Liquid spilled into the shifter causing leakage to ground

P092D.d: The module sees a higher voltage on shift lock circuit B than the commanded state allows, such as a short to supply or, with a low-side driver, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Lever will not release from its locked position
Fault appears intermittently with vibration
Warning message about the shifter or transmission
c: Circuit B wire shorted to a supply voltage
Poor crimp or loose terminal at the second lock solenoid
Open coil in the second lock solenoid

P0930.d: The voltage on control circuit A of the shift lock solenoid stays below the expected level, typically a short to ground or a driver output pulled low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Selector lever stuck in Park although the brake is pressed
Selector can be moved out of Park without pressing the brake
Shift lock override slot needed to move the lever
c: Shift lock control wire chafed through to ground in the console or under the carpet
Shorted turns in the shift lock solenoid coil
Spilled liquid in the shifter area causing leakage to ground

P0931.d: The control module reads a voltage on shift lock circuit A that is higher than the commanded state allows. FCA documents the code directly: in recall 16V-249 the Jefferson North plant found 2016 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles with active or stored P0931-00 whose selector would not release from Park.
s: Selector lever will not release from Park
Lever may lock in Park or Neutral unexpectedly after stopping
Fault comes and goes with vibration or temperature
c: Poorly crimped or loose terminal on the shift lock solenoid harness (FCA recall 16V-249)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open shift lock solenoid coil seen as high voltage by a low-side driver

P0932.d: General electrical fault in the circuit of the sensor that reports hydraulic pressure in the gearbox, usually line pressure in an automatic or system pressure in an automated manual or dual-clutch unit. The module sees a signal it cannot use at all, without a clear low or high pattern.
s: Warning light or transmission warning on
Harsh engagements and firm shifts from maximum line pressure
Possible limp mode with limited gears
c: Fault in the solenoid pack or valve body module that carries the pressure sensor (open solenoid, internal lead frame)
Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector terminals
5 V reference or sensor ground interrupted
Transmission or powertrain control module fault

P0933.d: The pressure reading is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state. Chrysler RFE, RLE and TES transmissions set it when measured line pressure is more than 25 psi (172 kPa) above the commanded value while staying below the highest pressure ever used in that gear; Sonnax notes that a maximum-pressure condition from an open pressure control solenoid circuit can trigger it and mislead toward the sensor.
s: Harsh or firm engagements and shifts
Warning light on
Shift quality does not adapt and may stay rough
c: Open circuit or fault in the line pressure control solenoid causing real excess pressure
Pressure sensor drifting or reading offset
Worn or sticking valves in the valve body
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid

P0934.d: The pressure sensor signal sits below its valid window. Chrysler RFE transmissions feed the line pressure sensor with a 5 V reference and expect 0.35 to 4.75 V; P0934 sets when the signal stays at or below 0.35 V for 0.18 s, monitored continuously with the engine running.
s: Warning light on
Harsh shifts due to default maximum pressure
Possible limp mode
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Pressure sensor or the solenoid pack carrying it failed

P0935.d: The pressure sensor signal sits above its valid window. On Chrysler RFE transmissions the line pressure sensor normally reads between 0.35 and 4.75 V; P0935 sets when the signal stays at or above 4.75 V for 0.18 s with the engine running.
s: Warning light on
Harsh shifts and engagements
Possible limp mode
c: Sensor ground open or poor terminal contact
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor or solenoid pack failed internally

P0936.d: The hydraulic pressure signal drops out or jumps for short periods, too briefly or irregularly for a lasting low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning light comes and goes
Occasional harsh or erratic shifts
c: Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault

P0937.d: General electrical fault in the circuit of the temperature sensor for the hydraulic fluid of an automated gearbox, without a clear low or high pattern. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Gearbox warning light on
Rougher shifts or clutch engagement, especially when cold
c: Connector at the temperature sensor loose, corroded or oil-soaked
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox or cooler lines

P0938.d: By J2012 wording the hydraulic oil temperature reading is electrically valid but implausible, for example frozen, rising too slowly after a cold start or disagreeing with other temperature values. Ferrari uses P0938 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, but describes it in its bulletin as no signal, an electrical fault rather than a plausibility check; the code is read in the NC
s: Gearbox warning light on
Shift and clutch quality inconsistent with operating temperature
c: Temperature sensor drifting or reacting sluggishly
Signal lost through connector or wiring fault (as in Ferrari's no-signal case)
Real temperature anomaly from a cooler or thermostat fault

P0939.d: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits below its valid window. With the usual NTC thermistor, a low voltage corresponds to an implausibly hot reading and typically comes from a signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor shorted internally.
s: Gearbox warning or overheat message
Reduced performance or altered shift behaviour
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground

P093A.d: The control circuit of the solenoid that opens or locks a hydraulic accumulator in the gearbox is open. Such accumulators store pressurised fluid, for example to keep clutches applied during engine stop-start, as GM's patents on a stop-start accumulator and an accumulator with solenoid valve describe.
s: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Jolt or slip when driving off after an engine restart
c: Connector unplugged or wire broken between module and solenoid
Fault in the internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

P093B.d: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads low, usually a control wire shorted to ground or a coil with very low resistance. No manufacturer documents P093B publicly.
s: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Harsh engagement after restart
c: Solenoid control wire shorted to ground
Output driver in the control module failed

P093C.d: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads high, typically a control wire shorted to battery voltage so the driver cannot switch the valve as commanded. No manufacturer documents P093C publicly.
s: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Jolt when pulling away after a restart
c: Solenoid control wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

P093D.d: The accumulator solenoid circuit is electrically sound, but the accumulator system does not deliver the expected hydraulic result. No manufacturer documents P093D publicly.
s: Engine stop-start disabled
Lurch or bang when the engine restarts
Firm shifts with adaptive learning frozen
c: Accumulator solenoid stuck open (drains) or closed (no fill)
Leakage at clutch seals or a worn valve body
Missing or misplaced check ball after a rebuild

P0940.d: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits above its valid window. With an NTC thermistor this matches an extremely cold reading, typically from an open circuit, an unplugged connector, a broken ground or a short to a voltage source.
s: Gearbox warning light on
Shifts or clutch engagements feel rough once warm
c: Open signal or ground wire, or connector unplugged
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

P0941.d: The hydraulic oil temperature signal jumps or drops out briefly, too short or irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Since fluid temperature changes slowly, a sudden step is a clear sign of an electrical problem rather than a real temperature change.
s: Warning light comes and goes
Shift quality varies unpredictably
c: Loose contact at the sensor connector under vibration or heat
Chafed wiring near hot gearbox or cooler parts
Sensor with an intermittent internal fault

P0942.d: General fault of the unit that generates and stores hydraulic pressure for an automated gearbox or its auxiliary oil supply: motor-driven pump, accumulator and pressure control. Toyota sets P0942 on the 2001 to 2005 MR2 Spyder sequential gearbox together with the SMT warning light and a buzzing pump, or with gears that can no longer be changed; fluid seeping from the reservoir cap or the seal of the hydraulic power u
s: Transmission or gearbox warning light on
Pump buzzing or running for long periods
Gears cannot be changed or shifts are delayed
Auto stop-start disabled or engine restarts immediately
c: Fluid loss at the reservoir cap or hydraulic power unit seals
Worn pump motor or faulty pump relay
Damaged wiring, connectors or power supply of the pump

P0943.d: In a hydraulic pressure unit the pump charges an accumulator up to a cut-out pressure and switches off until pressure falls to the cut-in point. By J2012 wording this code means the pump switches on again too soon, so the interval between charging cycles is shorter than expected.
s: Pump can be heard switching on unusually often
Warning light on
Slower or harsher gear changes
c: Accumulator has lost its gas precharge
Internal leakage at valves, seals or actuator cylinders
Faulty pressure switch or pressure sensor giving wrong cut-in point

P0944.d: The pump runs but the expected hydraulic pressure does not build or collapses. Stellantis names it Loss of Hydraulic Pump Prime: a 2023 STAR case lists it with P0868 and a slow engagement after the vehicle has stood, both set as the only transmission codes with the MIL on, and the fix was a new transmission; an FCA defect file from 2015 also shows it beside line pressure low.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow engagement after the vehicle has been parked
Auto stop-start not available or engine restarts at once
Slipping, no drive or limp mode
c: Pump loses prime (air drawn in through filter, seal or strainer pipe)
Blocked oil strainer or suction tube
Worn or failed pump (mechanical or electric)
Leaking check valve or internal leak in the valve body

P0945.d: The control module drives the motor of the hydraulic pump through a relay or a direct output. This code reports a general circuit fault or an open in that control path, so the pump cannot be switched reliably.
s: Warning light on
Pump does not run, pressure is not built
Gears cannot be changed or auto stop-start disabled
c: Pump relay coil open or relay not seated
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Failed output stage in the control module

P0946.d: The pump control circuit is electrically intact, but its behaviour does not match the command, for example a pump that keeps running after being switched off, or one that switches but is not followed by the expected feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Pump keeps running after switch-off
Warning light on
Auto stop-start not available
Battery discharged after parking
c: Pump supply or control wire shorted to battery voltage
Faulty pump state feedback or control module

P0947.d: The voltage on the control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver is lower than the module expects for the commanded state. Usually the line is shorted to ground or the relay coil is shorted, so the output may be overloaded and the pump runs when it should not, or the driver shuts down.
s: Warning light on
Pump runs continuously or not at all
Gearbox in limp mode or stop-start disabled
c: Relay control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Damaged output stage in the control module

P0948.d: The control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver shows a higher voltage than expected, typically because it is shorted to battery voltage or the relay coil is open on a low-side driver. The pump then cannot be switched on, or the module sees it as active when it is not.
s: Warning light on
Pump does not start
Gear changes not possible or stop-start disabled
c: Relay control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open relay coil seen as high level by the driver

P0949.d: Status code for an automatically shifted manual gearbox: the control unit has not yet finished learning its adaptation values, above all the clutch touch point and the end positions of the shift actuators. Such learning runs after a new control unit, clutch or actuator, after a software update and sometimes after the battery was disconnected; Hyundai and Kia patents show how the touch point is found and corrected fro
s: Jerky launch or rough shifts
Gearbox warning or message to perform teach-in
Restricted gear selection until learning completes
c: Relearn not run after clutch, actuator or control unit replacement
Adaptation values erased by software update or battery disconnection
Learning aborted by low voltage or worn clutch outside the learn window

P094A.d: Concerns the electronic driver that powers the motor of a hydraulic or electric oil pump, often a separate pump controller. The driver reports, or the module infers, that it cannot deliver the commanded speed or current although the circuit is not open or shorted.
s: Warning light on
Auto stop-start disabled
Delayed engagement or slower shifts
c: Internal fault of the pump controller or driver stage
Pump motor drawing excess current (worn bearings, fluid in motor)
High resistance in supply or ground of the driver

P094B.d: The hydraulic pump keeps running although the module has switched it off, or it never reaches its cut-out point. Causes are a welded relay or shorted driver, or a pump that cannot reach cut-out pressure because of leakage.
s: Pump audible after the vehicle is switched off
Discharged battery
Warning light on
c: Leakage or lost accumulator charge keeps pressure below cut-out
Shorted driver stage or supply wire shorted to battery voltage

P094C.d: The pump is commanded on but does not deliver: it does not turn, turns too slowly or produces too little pressure. The module judges this from pressure or speed feedback.
s: Warning light on
Engine restarts at once or stop-start not available
Delayed engagement or lost drive
c: Air in the pump after service or a suction leak
Blocked strainer or leaking check valve
Supply or relay fault stopping the pump

P094D.d: The hydraulic or electric oil pump, or its integrated controller, has become too hot. The temperature is usually measured on the controller board and the pump is derated or switched off to protect it.
s: Warning light on
Stop-start temporarily disabled
Burning smell near the pump in severe cases
c: Pump running too long because of leakage or a stuck relay
Very hot transmission fluid or blocked cooling

P094E.d: Fault in the power feed of the hydraulic or electric oil pump: fuse, supply wire, connector or relay output. The module sees missing or implausible supply at the pump or its controller.
s: Warning light on
Pump does not run
Stop-start disabled or gearbox in limp mode
c: Open or corroded supply wire or connector
Weak battery or poor main ground lowering pump supply voltage

P0950.d: General electrical fault in the circuit that carries the driver's manual up and down requests to the transmission control, as used by tip-shift gates on automatics and by automated manual gearboxes. A Chrysler patent shows the classic design: a transverse gate beside the drive positions with a proximity switch that signals upshift on one side and downshift on the other.
s: Manual or tip shifting does not respond
Gear display or warning message
Automatic mode still works normally
c: Failed up/down switch or sensor in the selector lever or paddles
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter (e.g. after spilled liquid)
Clockspring or steering column wiring fault on paddle-shift vehicles

P0951.d: Plausibility fault in the circuit that reports the driver's manual upshift and downshift requests, typically the tip gate of an automatic selector lever or steering wheel paddles. The signal is electrically valid but makes no sense, for example both requests active together or a request held far longer than any tap.
s: Tip shifting or paddles do not respond or respond erratically
Unwanted gear changes in manual mode
Warning message, automatic mode keeps working
c: Sticking or worn up/down tip switch, request signal stays active
Displaced magnet or damaged Hall sensor board in the selector lever
Spilled liquid or dirt in the shifter causing cross-talk between contacts
Faulty input stage in the transmission or shifter control module

P0952.d: The control unit sees the voltage on the manual up/down request circuit below its expected window, typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch stuck in the grounded state. In many tip gates the moving contact switches to ground, as a Nissan patent shows, so a short to ground can mimic a permanently held request; a Volkswagen patent describes checking the Hall tip sensors for shorts and breaks while the leve
s: Manual tip shifting inoperative
Gear indicator shows no manual gear or a warning message
Normal automatic driving in D still possible
c: Signal wire of the up/down circuit chafed through and shorted to ground
Tip switch stuck in the closed position
Moisture or spilled drink in the shifter creating a leakage path to ground
Low supply voltage to a Hall-type tip sensor

P0953.d: Voltage on the manual up/down request circuit lies above its expected window. Common reasons are a signal wire shorted to battery voltage or, where the input is pulled up internally, a broken wire or a switch that never closes.
s: Tip gate or paddles have no effect
Warning or message about manual mode
Automatic shifting continues normally
c: Signal wire shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the shifter harness
Broken wire or unplugged connector on a pulled-up input
Missing ground of the tip switch or Hall sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0954.d: The manual up/down request signal drops out or flickers for short moments, so a single tap may arrive twice, late or not at all. Unlike P0952 and P0953 the voltage is not stuck outside its window; it jumps between states without a matching lever movement.
s: Manual shifts occasionally ignored or executed twice
Fault comes and goes, often over bumps
Manual mode temporarily switched off
c: Loose or spread pins in the selector lever connector
Harness broken internally where it moves with the lever or steering column
Worn or oxidised tip switch contacts

P0955.d: Fault in the circuit that tells the transmission control whether the driver has moved the selector lever from D into the manual gate. A Nissan patent shows a dedicated manual mode switch with two contacts on separate inputs, so a break or a short to ground can be told apart; a Hyundai patent uses a microswitch on the lever.
s: Manual mode cannot be selected or is not displayed
Check engine or transmission warning light on
Driving in D remains possible
c: Failed manual mode switch or microswitch in the selector lever
Corroded or loose connector at the selector lever assembly
Damaged wiring between selector lever and transmission control module

P0956.d: The manual mode signal is electrically valid but contradicts other information, for example manual mode reported while the range sensor reads P, R or N, or the mode switch never changing although the up/down requests arrive. A Hyundai patent uses a microswitch with two opposing contacts and treats identical or missing signals on both inputs as a defect; a Nissan patent likewise compares two contacts of the manual mod
s: Manual mode drops out or will not engage
Display shows manual mode while lever is in D, or the reverse
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
c: Mode switch or its actuating foot misaligned on the lever
Worn switch contacts giving contradictory states on both inputs
Transmission range sensor out of adjustment, disagrees with the mode signal
Worn selector lever bushings allowing side play

P0957.d: Voltage in the manual mode circuit, the signal that reports the selector lever in the manual gate, is below the expected range. Mostly the signal line has a short to ground or the switch contact hangs in its grounded position.
s: Manual mode not available or permanently indicated
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
Automatic driving in D unaffected
c: Mode signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Mode switch stuck in the grounded position
Liquid or dirt in the selector lever housing

P0958.d: The manual mode signal from the selector lever reads above its expected range. Possible causes are a short to supply voltage or, with an internally pulled-up input, an open circuit or missing switch ground that keeps the line high.
s: Manual gate has no effect, gearbox stays in automatic mode
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
No manual gear shown on the display
c: Broken mode signal wire or disconnected shifter plug
Missing ground at the mode switch
Mode signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire

P0959.d: The signal reporting the selector lever in the manual gate drops out or toggles briefly while the lever is not moved, so the transmission control switches between manual and automatic mode on its own. The voltage is not stuck out of range as with P0957 or P0958 but jumps.
s: Manual mode switches on or off by itself
Gear display flickers between D and manual gear
Fault often appears on rough roads
c: Loose pins in the selector lever connector
Harness damaged where it moves with the lever

P095A.d: Circuit C is a third channel reporting the shift position inside an automated manual gearbox, for example a further sensor track or a sensor on another shift rail or selector shaft. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault of that signal that fits none of the more specific C variants.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral
c: Loose or corroded connector at shift position sensor C
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit C
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

P095B.d: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit C of an automated manual gearbox. The voltage is electrically acceptable, but the value does not fit: it contradicts the other position channels, stays put while the shift actuator moves, or misses the learned gear positions.
s: Transmission warning light on
Harsh or aborted gear changes
Fallback mode with fewer available gears
c: Worn or drifting shift position sensor C disagreeing with the other channels
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

P095C.d: The signal of shift position sensor C in an automated manual gearbox lies below its permitted voltage window. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a sensor with an internal fault pulling its output down.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Gearbox may refuse to leave neutral
c: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
Open or shorted 5 V supply of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

P095D.d: Shift position sensor C of an automated manual gearbox delivers a voltage above its permitted window. This usually points to a signal wire shorted to the supply, a broken sensor ground or, with a pulled-up input, an interrupted signal line.
s: Transmission or engine warning light on
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Jerky or aborted gear changes
c: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to the 5 V supply or battery voltage
Open ground circuit of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

P0960.d: Open-circuit fault in the driver circuit of pressure control solenoid A: the module measures an impedance far above the coil value, as if a wire, pin or winding were broken. Which solenoid carries the letter A depends on the gearbox.
s: Transmission warning or MIL on, fault message in the cluster
Very firm or harsh shifts due to maximum line pressure
Transmission stays in a fixed limp gear
c: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body or solenoid assembly
Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the transmission connector or pass-through
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module

P0961.d: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid does not behave as commanded. On GM's six-speeds, where A is the line pressure solenoid, the Saab 9-4X 6T70 sets it when measured and commanded current differ for 5 s, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s; both Type B, two trips.
s: Harsh or erratic shifts
MIL or transmission warning after the second drive
Slipping or ratio flare on CVT applications
c: Solenoid with internal electrical or mechanical fault, current no longer follows the command
Debris or varnish in the fluid sticking the solenoid or regulator valve
High resistance at connector or pass-through distorting the current
Low fluid level causing pressure errors (CVT pulley monitor)

P0962.d: Pressure control solenoid A circuit low: the driver sees a short to ground. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid this way; a short there opens a high-side switch that cuts power to the shift solenoids and leaves park, reverse, neutral and one fixed forward gear at maximum line pressure.
s: MIL and transmission warning on immediately
Limp mode with only one forward gear and reverse
Harsh engagements, poor acceleration from standstill
c: Control wire chafed through and touching ground
Transmission fluid or water in the connector bridging pins
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0963.d: Pressure control solenoid A circuit high: the driver detects a short to voltage, and on GM's six-speeds also an open circuit, since those units have no separate open code. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (line pressure solenoid) sets it after 5 s as Type B, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s over two trips; the module then commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations.
s: Firm or harsh shifts at maximum line pressure
Warning light, on some vehicles only after two drives or not at all
Shift adaptation no longer improves
c: Open coil or high-resistance connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated connector at the transmission
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0964.d: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid B. What B controls differs by gearbox: GM's 8-speed uses it for clutch 2 (CB12345R), the 9-speed for CB29 and the 10-speed for CB128910R, Allison 1000 for pressure control solenoid 2, and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the even-clutch pressure valve.
s: MIL and transmission warning on
Certain gears missing or limp mode
Dual-clutch gearbox drives on one sub-gearbox only
c: Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0965.d: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid B: wiring is intact, but current or resulting pressure does not match the command. In the Saab 9-4X 6T70, solenoid 2 feeds the 3-5-reverse clutch; a current mismatch for 5 s sets a Type C code without MIL and freezes that clutch's adaptations, and GM's 2016 six-speed table also lists it without MIL.
s: Rough or delayed 3rd, 5th or reverse engagement
CVT ratio fluctuates, engine speed flares
Often no warning light on six-speed applications
c: Worn or internally faulty solenoid, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or its regulator valve
Internal leak in the CVT primary pulley circuit
High resistance in connector or pass-through

P0966.d: Pressure control solenoid B circuit low, meaning a short to ground in the driver circuit. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch; a short lasting 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) or 1 s (Saab) sets a Type A code with a fixed limp mode: reverse and 5th gear, maximum line pressure, converter clutch off.
s: MIL on immediately
Limp mode with reverse and one forward gear
No torque converter lock-up, higher fuel consumption
c: Internally shorted solenoid in the valve body assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0967.d: Pressure control solenoid B circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, since they have no P0964. For the Saab 9-4X 6T70, where B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch, the module needs 1 s, stores a Type A code and limits the transmission to reverse and 3rd gear at maximum line pressure; GM's 2018 six-speed table uses 0.3 s and one trip.
s: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Dual-clutch gearbox loses the even gears
c: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0968.d: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip.
s: MIL and transmission warning on
Gears that need clutch C are unavailable
Limp mode in a fixed gear
c: Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0969.d: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve.
s: Usually no warning light
Rougher shifts into 4th, 5th, 6th or reverse over time
Shift adaptation stops learning
c: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve
High resistance in the internal connection to the module

P0970.d: Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches.
s: MIL on immediately
Limp mode in reverse and one forward gear
Weak acceleration from standstill
c: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0971.d: Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure.
s: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Fault comes and goes with temperature or vibration
c: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty output stage in the control module

P0972.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code.
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Transmission falls back to a fixed default gear
Missing or abrupt shifts
c: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage)
Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness
Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0973.d: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s.
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip on many vehicles
Limp mode with only a few gears, often reverse plus one forward gear
Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure
Torque converter lockup and manual shifting disabled
c: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly
Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector
Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module

P0974.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker.
s: MIL on, on GM six-speeds only after a second faulty trip
First gear locked out, start-off in a higher gear
Missing or wrong shifts, possibly limp mode
c: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0975.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely.
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Unexpected shift to neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
Fixed default gear or harsh shifts
c: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall)
Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B
Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0976.d: Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure.
s: Warning light or stored code, on some GM six-speeds without MIL
Firm shifts due to raised line pressure
Gears missing or limp mode
c: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing
Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly
Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector
Faulty driver in the transmission control module

P0977.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip.
s: Limp mode with only reverse and one high forward gear
Weak acceleration from rest
MIL or transmission warning, depending on calibration
c: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high
Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply
Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0978.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo.
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Sudden neutral or default gear while driving
Erratic or missing shifts
c: Intermittent high resistance at crimped harness terminals (FCA 9-speed)
Open coil of shift solenoid C (Allison-type usage)
Transmission software that predates the manufacturer's fix
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0979.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A).
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Transmission holds a default gear
Rough or delayed shifts involving the affected clutch
c: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body
Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

P097A.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open.
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Transmission in a fixed default gear
Shifts involving solenoid A missing
c: Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

P097B.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open.
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Default gear operation, some ranges unavailable
Harsh or missing shifts
c: Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit
Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P097C.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip.
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Upper gears unavailable or fixed default gear
Possible additional pressure switch code
c: Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid C
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

P097D.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly.
s: Warning light or MIL on
Missing gears that depend on solenoid D
Limp mode in a fixed gear
c: Open coil of shift solenoid D
Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit
Broken wire in the transmission harness
Faulty driver in the control module

P097E.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code.
s: Warning light or MIL on
Gears using solenoid E unavailable
Default gear operation
c: Open coil of shift solenoid E
Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame
Broken signal wire to solenoid E
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P097F.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block.
s: Warning light or MIL on
Gears that need solenoid F unavailable
Limp mode
c: Open coil of shift solenoid F
Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid F
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P0980.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip.
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Solenoid C stuck energized, wrong gear or default gear
Harsh shifts
c: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance
Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0981.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it.
s: Unexpected shift to neutral while driving (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Default gear or harsh shifts
c: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55)
Transmission software not yet updated by the recall
Solenoid D coil resistance out of range
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0982.d: Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s.
s: MIL on and default gear operation
No engine braking in first or no reverse, depending on gearbox
Harsh shifts into upper gears
c: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly
Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission
Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module

P0983.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765.
s: MIL on, default gear
Clunk or tie-up feel if the low/reverse clutch applies unintentionally
Upper gears blocked
c: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply
Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module

P0984.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford checks SSE with P0770, P0985 and P0986 only, GM's documented tables never reach letter E, and even Ferrari's DCT list, which reuses most of its neighbours, skips P0984.
s: Sudden neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Limp mode
c: Range sensor harness with weak crimps (FCA 9-speed recall)
TCM software below the recall level
Internal transmission fault when the code returns after the update
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0985.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford lists it for SSE on the 5R110W and 6R140 and in its 2020–2023 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries, beside P0770 for an open; for the 6R80 and 6F, whose SSE is the on/off multiplex solenoid, the 2012 text names only P0770.
s: MIL on after the fault is confirmed
All solenoids off, fixed fail-safe gear (Saab/Aisin)
Missing upper gears on Ford gearboxes
c: Solenoid E control wire shorted to ground
Water or fluid in the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module

P0986.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985.
s: MIL on, transmission in fail-safe gear
Tie-up or harsh shift if the controlled clutch stays applied
Adaptation frozen, shift quality worsens
c: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin)
Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P0987.d: General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning light depending on manufacturer
Harsher or less consistent shifts
Possible limp mode
c: Failed pressure sensor or switch E
Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0988.d: Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Often no noticeable symptom at first
Shift quality worsens because adaptation stops
Warning light depending on manufacturer
c: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all
Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve
Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit

P0989.d: Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released.
s: No warning light, code stored only
Shifts into 4th to 6th or reverse gradually less smooth
Occasional limp mode if the fault persists
c: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module
Debris keeping pressure away from the switch

P0990.d: Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch.
s: No warning light, code stored only
Intermittent occurrence without noticeable symptoms
Shift quality declines over time
c: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris
R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised
Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module

P0991.d: The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional harsh or flared shift
Shift adaptation frozen
c: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector
Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker
Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration
Fault in the transmission control module input stage

P0992.d: General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found.
s: Warning light depending on manufacturer calibration
Harsh or delayed shifts
Possible limp mode with a fixed gear
c: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch
Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module

P0993.d: Pressure sensor or switch F is electrically intact, but its reading does not match what the module expects from the commanded clutch state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Harsh or flared shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Warning light depending on calibration
c: Sticking clutch regulator valve feeding the switch
Worn or delaminated switch film, debris in the switch

P0994.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode
c: Switch stuck closed by debris or damaged film
Clutch circuit not reaching pressure (valve or seal leak)

P0995.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays high: with a normally closed switch the contacts stay open, which looks like permanent pressure, or the wire is open or shorted to voltage. No manufacturer documents this use publicly.
s: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode
c: Open signal wire or unplugged connector
Switch stuck open inside the valve body module

P0996.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F drops out or flickers for short moments without staying low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no transmission with a sixth pressure switch was found: GM's six-speeds end at switch 5 (E), Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses letters B, D and E.
s: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional rough or flared shift
c: Debris or delaminated film making the switch chatter
Chafed harness shorting or opening under vibration

P0997.d: The drive circuit of shift solenoid F works electrically but its measured current or voltage does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code.
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Missing or harsh shifts into gears using this solenoid
Possible limp mode
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

P0998.d: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid F. Two makers document it.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh engagement or flare when shifting
c: Solenoid or valve body (control valve) internal fault
Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector

P0999.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid F, from a short to voltage or, where the driver uses a pull-up, an open coil or wire. Nissan's bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT names P0999 together with P0998 as shift solenoid F and calls for replacing the control valve rather than the whole CVT when diagnosis confirms the fault.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh shifts
c: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Open control wire or short to voltage
Connector pin pushed out or corroded

P099A.d: The drive circuit of shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but current or voltage feedback does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code.
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid
Possible limp mode
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

P099B.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic uses it for the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with transmission relay voltage at 2 V or more and the solenoid commanded on, the module sets P099B if the actual voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s.
s: Check engine light
No reverse or no engine braking in first gear (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode
c: Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Shorted solenoid inside the valve body

P099C.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses P099C for an open circuit of the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with the solenoid commanded off and transmission relay voltage of 2 V or more, a reading of 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s sets the code.
s: Check engine light
No reverse or harsh reverse engagement (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode
c: Open control wire or connector between module and valve body
Open solenoid coil inside the valve body

P099D.d: Electrical feedback from the drive circuit of shift solenoid H does not fit the command, although no hard short or open is seen. No manufacturer was found to document this code.
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

P099E.d: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid H. No manufacturer was found to document this code.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P099F.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid H, from a short to voltage or, on pull-up driver designs, an open coil or wire. No manufacturer was found to document this code.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A0.d: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid G. It is a late addition to J2012: older code lists still show P09A0 to P09FF as reserved.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears
c: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Pin backed out of the connector housing

P09A1.d: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid H, the eighth shift solenoid. Like P09A0 it is a late J2012 addition that older code lists still show as reserved.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears
c: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Pin backed out of the connector housing

P09A2.d: General electrical fault on the second gate select position signal (circuit B) of an automated manual gearbox. The published designs from Isuzu (one select potentiometer) and Aisin AI (one select stroke sensor) show only a single sensor, so it is not documented whether B is a redundant second track of that sensor or a separate sensor.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox shifts slowly or locks out certain gears
Gearbox stays in one gear or neutral
c: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken signal wire of circuit B near the gearbox
Faulty select sensor, often integrated in the shift and select actuator
Faulty input stage for circuit B in the transmission control module

P09A3.d: Plausibility fault of gate select circuit B: the signal is electrically valid but does not match what the module expects. That could be the reading of circuit A, the learned gate positions, or the target gate the module has commanded, as in the Aisin AI select control that compares actual and target gate.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gate selected or gears refused
Slow, jerky shifting in fallback mode
c: Worn or drifting select sensor, signal B no longer agrees with the reference
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or module replacement
Contact resistance at connector pins distorting signal B
Sluggish or worn select mechanism so the measured gate lags the commanded one

P09A4.d: Set when the gate select signal on circuit B stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Likely causes are a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor short; with potentiometer sensors like the select position sensor in an Isuzu patent, an open signal wire often reads low too.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear changes blocked or limited to a few gears
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster
c: Signal wire of circuit B chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal short or broken wiper in the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P09A5.d: Indicates that the gate select signal on circuit B has stayed above its highest valid value for longer than allowed. Typical reasons are a short of the signal wire to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or a defective sensor.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Limp-home mode with very limited gear choice
c: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P09A6.d: Electrical fault on a third gate select position signal (circuit C) that fits none of the more specific C codes. Public AMT designs show far fewer channels: Aisin AI and Isuzu use one select sensor, and a Mannesmann Sachs patent combines motor encoders with an extra neutral position sensor.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Delayed or missing gear changes
Vehicle reluctant to pull away
c: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Damaged signal wire of circuit C in the gearbox harness
Faulty input stage for circuit C in the transmission control module

P09A7.d: Rationality fault on gate select circuit C: the value is electrically valid, yet it disagrees with the other select channels, the learned gate positions or the commanded movement. A Mannesmann Sachs patent shows why several select signals can exist: when one sensor fails, the remaining ones still allow controlled positioning before an emergency mode based on stored drive times takes over.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slower or hesitant gear changes
Some gears no longer offered
c: Drifting or worn sensor so signal C disagrees with the other channels
Select positions not relearned after repair work on the actuator or gearbox
Loose sensor mounting or magnet shifting the measured position
Contact resistance in the connector of circuit C

P09A8.d: The module stores this code when the gate select signal on circuit C remains below its valid range for a calibrated time. Common triggers are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or an internal sensor fault; depending on the sensor type, a broken signal wire can read low as well.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox holds one gear or drops to neutral
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster
c: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to ground
Sensor supply for circuit C missing or pulled down
Internal short in the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P09A9.d: Logged when the gate select signal on circuit C sits above its highest plausible value for longer than a calibrated time. Usual suspects are a short to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor with an internal fault.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Limp-home mode, often in a single low gear
Gear changes refused while driving
c: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to supply or battery voltage
Internal fault of the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
